title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    1| from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors
    2| import numpy as np
    3| 
    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.
   23| 
   24| ## Installation
   25| 
   26| ```bash
   27| git clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git
   28| cd TokenCore
   29| pip install -r requirements.txt
   30| ```
   31| 
   32| ## Quick Start
   33| 
   34| ```python
   35| from TokenCore import TextCore
   36| 
   37| model = TokenCore()
   38| 
   39| # Fit on normal token embeddings
   40| model.fit(X_train)
   41| 
   42| # Get token-level anomaly scores
   43| scores = model.decision_function(X_test)
   44| ```
   45| 
   46| `X_train` and `X_test` are token embedding matrices (e.g. BERT embeddings with max-pooling over subwords). See `Demo.ipynb` for the full pipeline, including embedding extraction, token-level scoring, and document-level aggregation.
   47| 
   48| ## Repository Structure
   49| 
   50| ```
   51| TokenCore/
   52| ├── data/           # Benchmark datasets (also on Hugging Face Hub)
   53| ├── TokenCore.py     # TokenCore method implementation
   54| ├── Demo.ipynb      # End-to-end demo of the key steps
   55| └── README.md
   56| ```
   57| 
   58| ## Citation

"""Load the released Grammar benchmark and reproduce the authors' train/test split.

Data source: repo/data/grammar.npy (released with the authors' repo), which is the
.npy mirror of repo/data/grammar_correction_labeled.json (Label Studio export).

The split logic in `split_anomaly_data` replicates the authors' eval.py, recovered
verbatim from the compiled bytecode eval.cpython-310.pyc (CPython 3.10, timestamp
2025-11-03) found in the shared data cache: defaults train_ratio=0.5,
random_state=42; n_train = int(len(X) * train_ratio) sampled WITHOUT replacement
from the NORMAL document indices only; test = setdiff1d(arange(len(X)), train).
"""
import numpy as np

N_DOCS = 300
N_ANOMALOUS_DOCS = 30


def load_grammar(path):
    """Return dict with tokens, labels, sentences, doc_labels; assert R10/R11."""
    data = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens = list(data["tokens"])
    labels = [list(l) for l in data["labels"]]
    sentences = list(data["sentences"])
    n = len(tokens)
    for t, l in zip(tokens, labels):
        assert len(t) == len(l), f"token/label length mismatch: {len(t)} vs {len(l)}"
    # R11: a document is anomalous iff it contains at least one anomalous token
    doc_labels = [1 if any(l) else 0 for l in labels]
    n_anom = sum(doc_labels)
    # R10: 300 documents, 270 normal + 30 anomalous (10% anomaly rate)
    assert n == N_DOCS, f"expected {N_DOCS} docs, got {n}"
    assert n_anom == N_ANOMALOUS_DOCS, f"expected {N_ANOMALOUS_DOCS} anomalous docs, got {n_anom}"
    return {
        "tokens": tokens,
        "labels": labels,
        "sentences": sentences,
        "doc_labels": doc_labels,
    }


def split_anomaly_data(X, y, z, train_ratio=0.5, random_state=42):
    """Authors' split, replicated statement-for-statement from their eval.py.

    X: list of per-document token lists (docs)
    y: document-level labels (0 normal / 1 anomalous)
    z: list of per-document token label lists
    """
    y = np.array(y)
    n_train = int(len(X) * train_ratio)
    normal_indices = np.where(y == 0)[0]
    np.random.seed(random_state)
    train_indices = np.random.choice(normal_indices, size=n_train, replace=False)
    test_indices = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(X)), train_indices)
    X_train = [X[i] for i in train_indices]
    y_train = y[train_indices]
    X_test = [X[i] for i in test_indices]
    y_test = y[test_indices]
    z_train = [z[i] for i in train_indices]
    z_test = [z[i] for i in test_indices]
    return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test

"""BERT-base-uncased word-level embedding extraction (paper Eq. 1, R1/R2/R9).

Reimplements the max-pooling logic of the authors' align.py::extract_word_embeddings
(same tokenizer call, same last_hidden_state, same np.max over stacked subword
vectors, special tokens skipped), but batched and quiet. One output unit per gold
word token, so units align 1:1 with the released token-level labels.
"""
import numpy as np
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel


class BertWordEmbedder:
    def __init__(self, model_path, batch_size=32, max_length=128):
        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path)
        self.model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_path)
        self.model.eval()
        self.device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
        self.model.to(self.device)
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.max_length = max_length

    def encode_docs(self, docs_tokens):
        """docs_tokens: list[list[str]] -> list[np.ndarray (n_tokens, 768)].

        Element-wise max pooling over each word's subword vectors (Eq. 1).
        [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] (word_id None) are excluded (R2/R9, A4).
        """
        all_emb = []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for start in range(0, len(docs_tokens), self.batch_size):
                batch = docs_tokens[start:start + self.batch_size]
                enc = self.tokenizer(
                    batch,
                    is_split_into_words=True,
                    return_tensors="pt",
                    truncation=True,
                    max_length=self.max_length,
                    padding=True,
                )
                enc = {k: v.to(self.device) for k, v in enc.items()}
                hidden = self.model(**enc).last_hidden_state.cpu().numpy()
                # word ids per batch element (recomputed on CPU side)
                enc_cpu = self.tokenizer(
                    batch,
                    is_split_into_words=True,
                    truncation=True,
                    max_length=self.max_length,
                    padding=True,
                )
                for i, tokens in enumerate(batch):
                    wids = enc_cpu.word_ids(batch_index=i)
                    groups = {}
                    for pos, wid in enumerate(wids):
                        if wid is None:
                            continue
                        groups.setdefault(wid, []).append(pos)
                    word_emb = np.stack(
                        [hidden[i, groups[wid]].max(axis=0) for wid in sorted(groups)]
                    )
                    # 1:1 alignment with the gold word tokens (R9)
                    assert word_emb.shape[0] == len(tokens), (
                        f"alignment broke: {word_emb.shape[0]} units vs "
                        f"{len(tokens)} gold tokens in doc {start + i}"
                    )
                    all_emb.append(word_emb.astype(np.float32))
        return all_emb

"""Thin adapter over the authors' unmodified TokenCore.py (repo/TokenCore.py).

Memory bank = all word-level embeddings of all tokens in the normal training
documents (R3); anomaly score = Euclidean distance to the nearest memory-bank
entry via sklearn NearestNeighbors defaults (R4, paper Eq. 2). No feature
scaling or normalization: StandardScaler is imported but never used anywhere in
the authors' compiled eval.py (A9).
"""
import os
import sys

REPO_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "repo")
if REPO_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_DIR)

from TokenCore import TokenCore  # noqa: E402  (authors' file, unmodified)


def fit_and_score(X_train, X_test, n_neighbors=1):
    """Fit the memory bank on normal-training token embeddings, score test tokens.

    n_neighbors=1 is the authors' benchmark config for TextCore/TokenCore
    (param grid {'n_neighbors': [1]} in their compiled eval.py).
    """
    clf = TokenCore(n_neighbors=n_neighbors)
    clf.fit(X_train)
    scores = clf.decision_function(X_test)
    return scores

"""Metric layer (R5/R7).

Token level: AUROC and AUPRC pooled over ALL test tokens of ALL test documents
(micro pooling), exactly as the authors' evaluate_model: roc_auc_score(y, s) and
auc(recall, precision) from precision_recall_curve. average_precision_score is
reported additionally as the more standard AUPRC variant.

Document level: per-document score = mean of the document's token scores
(paper Eq. 3, R5). The authors' compiled eval.py used np.max instead; both are
reported, with mean (the paper's specification) as the primary value.
"""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import (
    roc_auc_score,
    precision_recall_curve,
    auc,
    average_precision_score,
)


def auroc_auprc(y_true, scores):
    y_true = np.asarray(y_true)
    scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
    roc = roc_auc_score(y_true, scores)
    precision, recall, _ = precision_recall_curve(y_true, scores)
    prc_trapz = auc(recall, precision)  # authors' evaluate_model formula
    ap = average_precision_score(y_true, scores)
    return roc, prc_trapz, ap


def aggregate_doc_scores(token_scores, lengths, agg="mean"):
    """Split the flat per-token score array into documents and aggregate (Eq. 3)."""
    out = []
    start = 0
    for length in lengths:
        end = start + length
        seg = token_scores[start:end]
        if agg == "mean":
            out.append(float(np.mean(seg)))
        elif agg == "max":
            out.append(float(np.max(seg)))
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown aggregation {agg}")
        start = end
    assert start == len(token_scores)
    return np.array(out)

"""Reproduce TokenCore token-level AUROC/AUPRC on the Grammar dataset (C1/C2).

Pipeline (paper Sec. 5-6, claims C1/C2):
  1. Load the released Grammar benchmark (270 normal + 30 anomalous docs, R10).
  2. Authors' split (R6): n_train = int(300 * 0.5) = 150 normal docs chosen
     without replacement (np.random.seed(42) by default, from the authors'
     recovered eval.py), test = remaining 120 normal + 30 anomalous = 150 docs.
  3. BERT-base-uncased (R1) word-level embeddings via element-wise max pooling
     over each word's subword vectors (Eq. 1, R2), 1:1 with gold token labels.
  4. Memory bank from ALL tokens of the normal training documents (R3);
     token anomaly score = Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4).
  5. Token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro, R7);
     document-level scores by mean aggregation of token scores (Eq. 3, R5).

BERT embeddings are computed once for all 300 docs; the per-seed split, memory
bank and scoring take seconds, so multiple split seeds are reported cheaply.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SRC_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "src")
if SRC_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, SRC_DIR)

os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1")
os.environ.setdefault("TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE", "1")

from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_anomaly_data  # noqa: E402
from embed_bert import BertWordEmbedder  # noqa: E402
from detector import fit_and_score  # noqa: E402
from evaluate import auroc_auprc, aggregate_doc_scores  # noqa: E402

DEFAULT_SEEDS = [42, 0, 1, 2]  # 42 = the authors' recovered default; others = spread


def resolve_model_path(cache_dir):
    local = os.path.join(cache_dir, "models", "bert-base-uncased")
    if os.path.isdir(local) and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(local, "config.json")):
        return local
    return "bert-base-uncased"  # fall back to the HuggingFace hub id


def run_pipeline(docs, embedder, seed, smoke=False, verbose=True):
    tokens = docs["tokens"]
    labels = docs["labels"]
    doc_labels = docs["doc_labels"]

    if smoke:
        normal_idx = [i for i, d in enumerate(doc_labels) if d == 0][:8]
        anom_idx = [i for i, d in enumerate(doc_labels) if d == 1][:2]
        keep = sorted(normal_idx + anom_idx)
        tokens = [tokens[i] for i in keep]
        labels = [labels[i] for i in keep]
        doc_labels = [doc_labels[i] for i in keep]

    t0 = time.time()
    (X_train_tok, y_train, X_test_tok, y_test,
     z_train, z_test, train_idx, test_idx) = split_anomaly_data(
        tokens, doc_labels, labels, train_ratio=0.5, random_state=seed)

    # BERT forward pass once over the (sub)corpus, then select by doc index.
    emb_all = embedder.encode_docs(tokens)
    X_train = np.vstack([emb_all[i] for i in train_idx])   # memory bank (R3)
    X_test = np.vstack([emb_all[i] for i in test_idx])
    flat_z = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z, dtype=np.int64) for z in z_test])

    # --- intermediate checks -------------------------------------------------
    assert X_train.shape[1] == 768, f"expected 768-d embeddings, got {X_train.shape[1]}"
    assert X_train.shape[0] == sum(len(t) for t in X_train_tok), "bank size mismatch"
    assert X_test.shape[0] == sum(len(t) for t in X_test_tok), "test token count mismatch"
    assert not any(any(l) for l in z_train), "anomalous token leaked into the bank (R3)"
    assert X_test.shape[0] == len(flat_z)

    # --- TokenCore: memory bank + nearest-neighbour scoring ------------------
    scores = fit_and_score(X_train, X_test, n_neighbors=1)

    token_roc, token_prc_trapz, token_ap = auroc_auprc(flat_z, scores)

    lengths = [len(t) for t in X_test_tok]
    doc_scores_mean = aggregate_doc_scores(scores, lengths, agg="mean")   # Eq. 3 / R5
    doc_scores_max = aggregate_doc_scores(scores, lengths, agg="max")     # authors' eval.py variant
    y_test = np.asarray(y_test)
    doc_roc_mean, doc_prc_mean, doc_ap_mean = auroc_auprc(y_test, doc_scores_mean)
    doc_roc_max, _, _ = auroc_auprc(y_test, doc_scores_max)

    # --- random-score control (metric plumbing sanity) -----------------------
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    ctrl_scores = rng.random(len(flat_z))
    ctrl_roc, _, _ = auroc_auprc(flat_z, ctrl_scores)

              f"token AP={token_ap:.4f}")

        "seed": int(seed),
        "n_train_docs": int(len(train_idx)),
        "n_test_docs": int(len(test_idx)),
        "n_bank_tokens": int(X_train.shape[0]),
        "n_test_tokens": int(X_test.shape[0]),
        "n_positive_test_tokens": int(flat_z.sum()),
        "token_auroc": float(token_roc),
        "token_auprc_trapz": float(token_prc_trapz),
        "token_auprc_ap": float(token_ap),
        "doc_auroc_mean": float(doc_roc_mean),
        "doc_auprc_mean": float(doc_prc_mean),
        "doc_auprc_mean_ap": float(doc_ap_mean),
        "doc_auroc_max": float(doc_roc_max),
        "random_control_auroc": float(ctrl_roc),
        "runtime_seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 2),
    }

"""Diagnostic: compare cached embeddings to our pipeline and check AUROC sources.

NOT part of the reproduction — investigation only. Runs the authors' exact split
(seed 42) + TokenCore on: (a) our uncased embeddings, (b) cached flat uncased X,
(c) cached per-doc uncased npz, (d) cached per-doc cased npz; and measures how
close our extraction is to the cached ones.
"""
import os
import sys
import numpy as np

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "src"))
from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_anomaly_data  # noqa: E402
from detector import fit_and_score  # noqa: E402
from evaluate import auroc_auprc, aggregate_doc_scores  # noqa: E402

cache = os.environ["REPRO_DATA_CACHE"]
docs = load_grammar(os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "data", "grammar.npy"))
tokens, labels, doc_labels = docs["tokens"], docs["labels"], docs["doc_labels"]

(_, _, X_test_tok, y_test, _, z_test, train_idx, test_idx) = split_anomaly_data(
    tokens, doc_labels, labels, train_ratio=0.5, random_state=42)
flat_z = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z) for z in z_test])
lengths = [len(t) for t in X_test_tok]


def evaluate_flat(emb_all, tag):
    X_train = np.vstack([emb_all[i] for i in train_idx])
    X_test = np.vstack([emb_all[i] for i in test_idx])
    scores = fit_and_score(X_train, X_test, n_neighbors=1)
    tok_roc, tok_prc, tok_ap = auroc_auprc(flat_z, scores)
    dm = aggregate_doc_scores(scores, lengths, "mean")
    dx = aggregate_doc_scores(scores, lengths, "max")
    d_roc_m, _, _ = auroc_auprc(y_test, dm)
    d_roc_x, _, _ = auroc_auprc(y_test, dx)
    print(f"{tag:28s} token AUROC={tok_roc:.4f} AUPRC={tok_prc:.4f} "
          f"docAUROC(mean)={d_roc_m:.4f} docAUROC(max)={d_roc_x:.4f}")
    return scores


# (b) cached flat uncased
z = np.load(os.path.join(cache, "emb", "emb_bert-base-uncased_grammar_7bd3c33159_300.npz"),
            allow_pickle=True)
Xc, spans = z["X"], z["spans"]
emb_flat = [Xc[s:e] for s, e in spans]
evaluate_flat(emb_flat, "cached flat uncased")

# (c) cached per-doc uncased
z2 = np.load(os.path.join(cache, "grammar_emb", "bert-base-uncased.npz"), allow_pickle=True)
per_doc = z2["data"]
emb_pd_u = [d["emb"] for d in per_doc]
evaluate_flat(emb_pd_u, "cached per-doc uncased")

# (d) cached per-doc cased
z3 = np.load(os.path.join(cache, "grammar_emb", "bert-base-cased.npz"), allow_pickle=True)
emb_pd_c = [d["emb"] for d in z3["data"]]
evaluate_flat(emb_pd_c, "cached per-doc cased")

# (a) our embeddings
from embed_bert import BertWordEmbedder  # noqa: E402
model_path = os.path.join(cache, "models", "bert-base-uncased")
emb_ours = BertWordEmbedder(model_path).encode_docs(tokens)
evaluate_flat(emb_ours, "ours uncased")

# ---- closeness of extraction ----
our_flat = np.vstack(emb_ours)
cached_flat = np.vstack(emb_pd_u)
diff = np.abs(our_flat - cached_flat)
print(f"\nours vs cached per-doc uncased: max|d|={diff.max():.3e} mean|d|={diff.mean():.3e}")
cos = (our_flat * cached_flat).sum(1) / (np.linalg.norm(our_flat, axis=1) * np.linalg.norm(cached_flat, axis=1) + 1e-12)
print(f"cosine sim: min={cos.min():.6f} mean={cos.mean():.6f}")

flat_vs_pd = np.abs(np.vstack(emb_flat) - cached_flat)
print(f"cached flat vs cached per-doc uncased: max|d|={flat_vs_pd.max():.3e}")

cased_flat = np.vstack(emb_pd_c)
diff_c = np.abs(our_flat - cased_flat)
print(f"ours vs cached per-doc cased: max|d|={diff_c.max():.3e}")

"""One-at-a-time ablations of the paper-ambiguous scoring choices (plan step 13).

Baseline = the exact reproduce.py configuration:
  bert-base-uncased, max pooling over subwords (Eq. 1), raw Euclidean
  nearest-neighbour distance to the full normal-training memory bank (Eq. 2),
  punctuation units included, token-level AUROC pooled over all test tokens
  (micro), document scores = mean aggregation (Eq. 3).

Each variant changes exactly ONE choice:
  V_pool_perdoc : A5  - per-document token AUROC averaged over the test docs that
                        contain both classes, instead of one pooled ranking
  V_cosine      : A9/A1 - L2-normalize every embedding before bank/scoring, i.e.
                        cosine nearest-neighbour distance instead of raw Euclidean
  V_no_punct    : A4  - punctuation units (tokens without any [A-Za-z0-9] char)
                        excluded from the memory bank and from the test ranking

Every variant is evaluated on the plan seeds {0, 1, 2} plus the authors' code
default seed 42 as a reference row, each with a random-score control. Results go
to ablation_log.json (workspace root, outside results/).
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, precision_recall_curve, auc

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "src"))
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1")
os.environ.setdefault("TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE", "1")

from data_grammar import load_grammar, split_anomaly_data  # noqa: E402
from embed_bert import BertWordEmbedder  # noqa: E402
from detector import fit_and_score  # noqa: E402

SEEDS = [0, 1, 2, 42]  # plan seeds + authors' code default as reference
PUNCT_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9]")


def is_punct(tok):
    return PUNCT_RE.search(tok) is None


def pooled_metrics(y, scores):
    y = np.asarray(y)
    roc = roc_auc_score(y, scores)
    p, r, _ = precision_recall_curve(y, scores)
    return float(roc), float(auc(r, p))


def perdoc_auroc(z_test, scores, lengths):
    """Mean token-level AUROC computed inside each test doc that has both classes."""
    vals, pos = [], 0
    for doc_labels, doc_scores in zip(z_test, np.split(scores, np.cumsum(lengths)[:-1])):
        d = np.asarray(doc_labels)
        if d.sum() == 0 or d.sum() == len(d):
            continue  # single-class doc: AUROC undefined
        vals.append(roc_auc_score(d, doc_scores))
        pos += 1
    return float(np.mean(vals)), len(vals)


def main():
    docs = load_grammar(os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "data", "grammar.npy"))
    tokens, labels, doc_labels = docs["tokens"], docs["labels"], docs["doc_labels"]

    cache_dir = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join(ROOT, ".cache"))
    model_path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "models", "bert-base-uncased")
    if not os.path.isdir(model_path):
        model_path = "bert-base-uncased"
    embedder = BertWordEmbedder(model_path)
    emb_all = embedder.encode_docs(tokens)

    n_punct = sum(1 for t in tokens for w in t if is_punct(w))
    n_punct_pos = sum(1 for t, l in zip(tokens, labels)
                      for w, y in zip(t, l) if is_punct(w) and y == 1)
    print(f"punctuation units in corpus: {n_punct} "
          f"({n_punct_pos} of the {sum(sum(l) for l in labels)} anomalous tokens)")

    log = {"seeds": SEEDS, "punct_units_in_corpus": n_punct,
           "punct_positive_tokens": n_punct_pos, "variants": {}}
    ctrl_rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

    for variant in ["baseline", "V_pool_perdoc", "V_cosine", "V_no_punct"]:
        rows = []
        for seed in SEEDS:
            (_, _, X_test_tok, y_test, _, z_test, train_idx, test_idx) = split_anomaly_data(
                tokens, doc_labels, labels, train_ratio=0.5, random_state=seed)
            flat_z = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z) for z in z_test])
            lengths = [len(t) for t in X_test_tok]

target.statement: TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar dataset
target.table_ref: Table 1, Token section, row TokenCore, column Grammar ROC

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The reproduction implements TokenCore faithfully on the Grammar benchmark: bert-base-uncased last hidden state, element-wise max pooling over subwords via word_ids (embeddings match the authors' cached uncased embeddings to max|Δ|≈1e-4), a full bank of normal-training token embeddings, Euclidean 1-NN token scores, and mean document aggregation; per-seed random-score controls confirm the metric plumbing. The split follows the authors' compiled eval.py (150 normal docs via np.random.choice) rather than the paper's literal 50% of normal (135), which is disclosed in A13 and introduces no train/test leakage. Only this one condition was executed: neither the six baselines (LOF/iForest/ECOD/DeepSVDD/AutoEncoder/LUNAR) nor the Review or SMS_Spam datasets were run, so R8 and claims C3-C8 are absent even though implementer_scaled_down is null and the implementer summary says only 'run time budget reached'. The reported primary Grammar token AUROC is 0.5952 (multi-seed mean of seeds 0/1/2) versus the paper's 0.6371, a 0.042 gap outside the 0.02 tolerance; the per-seed AUROC spans 0.5633-0.6295 (seed 42 = 0.6137), so the paper's point estimate lies inside the seed-to-seed spread (seed 0 = 0.6295 is within tolerance) and the discrepancy is consistent with single-split randomness on only 47 positive tokens plus paper ambiguities (distance metric/normalisation, hidden layer, punctuation handling, per-document vs pooled AUROC, train-set size). Token AUPRC reproduces closely (0.0372 vs 0.0407), further supporting method fidelity, and no reported number is hard-coded or copied from the paper (paper_numbers_found_in_code is empty; the implementer did not cherry-pick the seed closest to the target). The run therefore answers the right question (Grammar token AUROC for TokenCore) and is not scaled down, but the primary multi-seed value falls short of the claim tolerance.

requirement_check.evidence: The implemented TokenCore pipeline uses bert-base-uncased last_hidden_state (metrics.json config; embed_bert.BertWordEmbedder imported by ablate_variants.py/diagnose_embeddings.py). Baselines are not implemented — that is tracked under R8.

Word vectors are formed by element-wise max pooling over subword vectors via word_ids (config: subword_to_word_pooling='element-wise max over subword vectors (Eq. 1)'). diagnose_embeddings.py shows the produced per-doc embeddings match the authors' cached uncased embeddings to max|Δ|≈1e-4, consistent with the same pooling.

split_anomaly_data samples train_indices from normal_indices only (np.where(y==0)); the bank is X_train built from those docs. Clean re-run shows '[seed 0] bank tokens: 1342' from 150 normal training docs; no anomalous-token embeddings are stored.

detector.fit_and_score(X_train, X_test, n_neighbors=1) with Euclidean distance; config: 'token_score': 'distance to nearest memory-bank entry (Eq. 2)', 'n_neighbors': 1, 'distance_metric': 'euclidean'.

Document scores are the mean of token scores (aggregate_doc_scores(..., 'mean'); per-seed doc_auroc_mean is the primary document value, and the authors' np.max aggregation is reported only as doc_auroc_max ablation).

Training set is n_train = int(300*0.5) = 150 normal docs (authors' compiled eval.py convention, recovered via xdis), i.e. 55.6% of the 270 normal documents, not the paper's literal 50% of normal (=135). Normal-only training and normal+anomalous test are preserved; disclosed in assumption A13, no train/test leakage.

Both metrics at both levels are computed: token AUROC and token AUPRC (auc(recall, precision) with precision_recall_curve, matching the authors' eval.py), plus document AUROC and document AUPRC (per_seed doc_auroc_mean/doc_auprc_mean). Random-score controls (~0.45-0.56) confirm the metric plumbing.

Only TokenCore is implemented. LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder and LUNAR are never run in reproduce.py, ablate_variants.py or diagnose_embeddings.py (the compiled authors' eval.py lists them, but no baseline results appear in metrics.json).

Scores are computed at the word level by pooling subwords with word_ids so they align one-to-one with the released word-level annotations (2746 tokens, 47 anomalous tokens); punctuation-attached word units are retained, matching the released annotation tokenisation (306 punctuation units, 0 of them anomalous).
Clean re-run: 'corpus: 300 docs, 2746 tokens, 47 anomalous tokens (1.71%), 30 anomalous docs'; grammar.npy gives 270 normal + 30 anomalous = 300, 10% anomaly rate.

Document labels z/doc_labels are the released sentence-level labels; the 30 anomalous documents (containing the 47 anomalous tokens) are all in the 150-document test set, so document labels are consistent with token labels.
